summary: Cathy Cantwell specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Kent (~1984–1989) and held a post at the University of Oxford in 2002.

Cecil Bendall was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Cambridge, Oxford, and under Edward Byles Cowell and Theodor Benfey. He held posts at the British Museum, University College London, and as Professor at Cambridge.

Cecil Y. Lang studied at Duke University (~1937–1941). He held appointments at Yale University (~1949–1951), the University of Chicago (~1965–1970), and served as Professor of English at the University of Virginia (~1970–1991).

Ch'ing-mao Cheng, a scholar of Sinology and Japanology, earned degrees from National Taiwan University and Princeton. He taught at UC Berkeley and UMass Amherst, and was Founding Chair at National Dong Hwa University (~1996–2003).

Chack-fan Lee, active in Buddhist studies and other fields, studied at the University of Hong Kong (~1964–1968) and the University of Western Ontario (~1970–1972). He served as Pro-Vice-Chancellor at the University of Hong Kong (1994–2015).
Chaeson Kim is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo (attested 1995) under Yasunori Ejima.

Chagdud Tulku Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure. He studied under traditional teachers including Delog Dawa Drolma, Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Tromge Trungpa Rinpoche, Khenpo Dorje, and Dilgo Khyentse.
Chaim Rabin was a linguist who studied at SOAS University of London and the University of Oxford. He held academic posts at Oxford (1941–1956) and the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (1956–1986).

Chaisit Suwanvarangkul is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who conducted research at Kyoto University and the University of Delhi. He served as a Lecturer in Buddhist Studies at the University of Otago (attested 2015).

Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad, working in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies, completed a doctorate at the University of Oxford. He held research fellowships at Oxford and Cambridge, taught at National University of Singapore, and became Professor at Lancaster University.

Chamnong Adivadhanasit is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned a BA from Chulalongkorn University. By 2012, he was a Professor at Kasetsart University and a part-time instructor at Chulalongkorn University.
Champa Thupten Zongtse is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at the University of Göttingen, attested in 1991 and as a Lecturer in 2009.

Chandra R. de Silva was a historian who served as Professor at the University of Peradeniya (attested 1991) and later as Dean of the College of Arts and Letters at Old Dominion University (attested 2006).

Chandrabhal Tripathi was an Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt. He worked at Göttingen and Cologne before serving as Professor at the Free University of Berlin (~1973–1994).
Chang-geun Hwang is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 2000, studying under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Minoru Kiyota, and Morten Schlütter.

Changhwan Park is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Otani University and UC Berkeley under Noritoshi Aramaki and Alexander von Rospatt. He served as Professor at Geumgang University (attested 2013–2017).

Changpei Luo was a linguist and Sinologist who studied at Peking University (~1916–1921). He held posts at Northwest University, Xiamen University, Sun Yat-sen University, and Peking University (~1931–1944).

Chanju Mun is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and studied at the University of Tokyo, supervised by Charles Hallisey, Morten Schlütter, and Masahiro Shimoda.
Channa Li is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Jonathan A. Silk (attested 2015) and was a PhD candidate at Leiden University (attested 2019).

Charlene Elizabeth Makley is a Tibetology and anthropology scholar who completed her PhD at the University of Michigan (1999) under Norma Diamond and Roy Rappaport. She became an associate professor of anthropology at Reed College.
